subject.title: [Feature]: Gateway RPCs for WhatsApp group management (whatsapp.groups.info / rename / participants add/remove)

question: Should OpenClaw expose mutable WhatsApp group management as a supported `whatsapp.groups.*` Gateway API, and if so which read/write operations and authorization safeguards are part of the initial contract?
rationale: The underlying library can perform these actions and plugin infrastructure can register Gateway methods, but choosing a permanent write-capable public channel API and its compatibility/security boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded channel API
options.body: Add group-info, rename, add, and remove methods in the existing WhatsApp channel with stable schemas, existing gateway authentication, narrow validation, and live admin-group proof.

options.title: Start read-only
options.body: Expose group metadata first and defer membership and rename mutations until maintainers settle write-operation safeguards and long-term API ownership.

options.title: Defer the public surface
options.body: Keep host-side automation as the supported workaround until a first-party workflow establishes the required capability contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded channel API
recommendation.body: Add group-info, rename, add, and remove methods in the existing WhatsApp channel with stable schemas, existing gateway authentication, narrow validation, and live admin-group proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision balances the repository’s plugin-first scope with the roadmap priority for major messaging-channel support.
